subject: dwarf reed snake
title: This Snake Escapes by Cartwheeling, 4 Times Faster Than It Slithers

scenes.text: This snake's fastest move isn't slithering. Not even close.
The dwarf reed snake of Southeast Asia is about a foot long. Birds and bigger snakes hunt it.
When one gets close, it throws its body into a loop and rolls away like a wheel.
Scientists filmed it in Borneo. Rolling, it hits up to twelve feet a second, about four times its slithering speed.
And it steers. The head stays level and pointed forward while the body spins behind it.
A snake with no legs worked out the cartwheel. Scientists only explained it in October 2026.

description:
The dwarf reed snake's fastest way to move is not slithering: when a predator closes in, it rolls away like a wheel.
A study in Current Biology (19 October 2026) filmed dwarf reed snakes (genus Pseudorabdion) in Sarawak, Borneo. Peak rolling speeds were 1.72 to 3.69 metres per second, about four times their peak slithering speed, and the snakes kept to a track just 20 centimetres wide with the head held level and facing forward.
Which animal has the strangest way of getting away? Comment below.
first_comment: It stays on a track only 20 centimetres wide while rolling at up to 3.69 metres a second. Would you believe it without the video?
